title: Verify Disbursement Charges Against Outside Counsel Billing Guidelines — Compliance Report

blind.coverage: I read all four supplied documents in full: the billing guidelines, the engagement letter, the pre-approval log, and the invoice XLSX (Summary, Professional Fees and Disbursements sheets). I also read the instructions and all 57 criteria. I recomputed the Disbursements sheet with a script: the 47 line items sum to $145,404.30. By category: Travel 3,788.30, Document Production 14,940, Expert/Consultant 76,800, Court Costs 511, Courier 159, Meals 1,001, Technology 20,395, Contract Attorneys 27,810. The Professional Fees lines sum to $161,698.50. I checked each criterion's facts, amounts and section references against the documents. No case law or statute controls the result, since this is interpretation of a private billing guideline, so I consulted no external legal sources and cite no authorities. I did not open the harness system prompt or judge prompt beyond the task description. I did not look at any other audit.

findings.title: Invoice lines sum to $145,404.30, not $86,742.30; the real discrepancy is $58,662.11, not $0.11
findings.explanation: C-041 passes only if the report finds a $0.11 gap between the stated total ($86,742.19) and a line-item sum of $86,742.30. The 47 amounts on the Disbursements sheet actually sum to $145,404.30. The Expert/Consultant lines alone ($76,800) plus Contract Attorneys ($27,810) come to $104,610, which is already above the stated total. G50 is a hardcoded value, not a formula. So a solver that adds the lines correctly will report a $58,662.11 understatement and fail C-041. Judges see only the criterion, not the spreadsheet, so they will treat $0.11 as correct. The Professional Fees sheet has the same kind of defect (lines sum to $161,698.50 against a stated $187,420), which suggests the subtotals were written separately from the line items. Only a solver that repeats the rubric's wrong arithmetic can pass.

evidence.quote: D50='TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS' | G50=86742.19
D23='Dr. Evelyn Hartsfield, statistical/econometric expert, compensation analysis, May invoice' | E23=1 | F23=32500 | G23=32500
does not match the sum of the 47 line items (which totals $86,742.30), resulting in an $0.11 discrepancy
Invoice totals must accurately reflect the sum of all individual line items.

findings.suggested_fix: Fix the record so the line items reconcile to the intended total, or rewrite C-041: 'PASS if the report identifies that the stated disbursement total ($86,742.19) does not equal the sum of the line items ($145,404.30), a discrepancy of $58,662.11.'

findings.title: Line 38 dinner was attended only by firm personnel, so §5.7 disallows all $612; C-034 requires a $357 partial reduction
findings.explanation: All five Line 38 attendees work for HWK: Aldridge, Beale, Palermo and two summer associates. No Pinnacle personnel or third-party witnesses were present. §5.7 says meals attended solely by firm personnel are not reimbursable, regardless of whether case work was discussed. The compliant amount is therefore $0 and the correct reduction is $612. C-034 wrongly treats the three HWK timekeepers as eligible (compliant amount 3 × $85 = $255) and fails any reduction more than $20 away from $357. That fails the correct answer. C-032 carries the same premise that only the summer associates are ineligible, though a solver who says every attendee is firm personnel probably still passes it. C-033 requires per-person cap math for a meal that is wholly non-reimbursable, so a solver that rejects it outright may fail.

evidence.quote: Meals attended solely by Firm personnel --- without Pinnacle personnel or third-party witnesses present --- are NOT reimbursable as disbursements, regardless of whether case-related work was discussed during the meal.
Working dinner, C. Aldridge, M. Beale, J. Palermo, and two summer associates, brief preparation at Carmichael's Steakhouse, Charlotte
arriving at a reduction of approximately $357 (compliant amount = 3 × $85 = $255; reduction = $612 − $255 = $357)... or the calculated reduction deviates from $357 by more than $20

findings.suggested_fix: Change C-034 to require rejecting all $612 because every attendee is HWK personnel under §5.7. Reword C-032 so it treats all attendees as ineligible, not just the summer associates. Make C-033 optional or an alternative ground.

findings.title: Line 40 dinner had at least three diners, so it was $82.33 per person, under the $85 cap; C-045 divides by two
findings.explanation: The invoice describes a dinner for C. Aldridge and M. Beale 'with plaintiff's counsel', which is at least three people. The time entry for the same day (fee line 62) confirms that plaintiff's counsel attended. $247 / 3 = $82.33, which is under the $85 dinner cap. C-045 requires the report to find $123.50 per person ($247 / 2) and an excess of $38.50 per person, a headcount the record contradicts. A careful solver will either find no per-person violation or reject the whole meal as entertainment or an ineligible attendee under §5.7. Either way it fails C-045. The $77 total excess matches $247 − 2 × $85 only by coincidence, and the PASS text is tied to the $123.50 figure.

evidence.quote: Working dinner, C. Aldridge and M. Beale, with plaintiff's counsel settlement discussion at The Piedmont Room
working dinner with M. Beale and plaintiff's counsel re settlement discussion
PASS if the report identifies that $247 / 2 = $123.50 per person exceeds the $85/person working dinner cap

findings.suggested_fix: Delete C-045, or rewrite it to accept either a full rejection of Line 40 or a cap analysis based on the actual number of attendees (at least 3).

findings.title: C-019 treats the $25K GC threshold as unmet, but GC Cha had already approved Hartsfield up to $35K/month
findings.explanation: The pre-approval log shows the General Counsel concurred in retaining Hartsfield with a $35,000 monthly cap, which already covers the $25,000 GC threshold. The real violation is the $5,900 above the approved cap. The approval email and the §5.4 budget-cap rule both require GC sign-off for that overage. C-019's wording suggests that $40,900 breaches a GC pre-approval requirement that was never met. Most solvers will mention that the overage needs GC authorization and will pass. A solver that says the $25K threshold was satisfied and frames the problem only as a cap overrun may fail.

evidence.quote: Because the anticipated monthly fees exceed the \$25,000 threshold under Section 5.4 of our Billing Guidelines, Lorraine\'s approval was required and has been obtained.
exceed the $25,000/month threshold requiring General Counsel (Lorraine Cha) pre-approval under Section 5.4. FAIL if this GC approval requirement is not mentioned.

findings.suggested_fix: Reword C-019: 'PASS if the report notes that the $5,900 above the GC-approved $35,000 cap required advance General Counsel authorization, which the log does not show.'

findings.title: C-052 requires a pending-approval total, but the guidelines also let a reviewer reject unapproved items outright
findings.explanation: The instructions ask for a compliance report with recommended reductions. §8.6 does describe holding charges while a retroactive-approval request is decided. But §5.1 and §5.4 say that charges incurred without pre-approval may be rejected in their entirety. A reviewer can reasonably recommend rejecting Voss, GraphicWorks, Brooks and DataScan outright, in which case the report has no pending bucket and fails C-052. The rubric is not consistent here: C-023, C-028 and C-040 accept 'at risk' or full rejection as alternatives. C-052, which requires a separate held-pending total, is less flexible.

evidence.quote: Failure to obtain Pre-Approval may result in rejection of the charge in its entirety.
FAIL if no pending-approval amount is provided.
rather than outright rejected (or alternatively flags the full $6,800 as at risk)

findings.suggested_fix: Let C-052 pass if the report either gives a held-pending total or clearly states a total for pre-approval failures, whether recommended for hold or for rejection.

findings.title: C-050 accepts only $86,742.19 or $86,742.30 as the billed total; the lines actually sum to $145,404.30
findings.explanation: Because of the O1 defect, a solver that reports total billed disbursements as the sum of the billed lines ($145,404.30) passes only if it also recites the invoice's stated $86,742.19. Most reports will quote the stated figure, but one that relies on the recomputed sum could fail. The criterion's reference to '$86,742.30 as the arithmetic sum' is simply wrong.

evidence.quote: approximately $86,742.19 as stated on the invoice or $86,742.30 as the arithmetic sum

findings.suggested_fix: Accept $86,742.19 (stated) or $145,404.30 (line-item sum), or fix the record.

blind.overall: Most of the rubric follows the guidelines and pre-approval log accurately: the hotel, photocopy, Westlaw, mileage, travel-meal, contract-attorney, e-discovery, courier and rental-car criteria are all correct. Three criteria would fail correct work. C-041 depends on a $0.11 total discrepancy that the spreadsheet does not contain: the 47 lines sum to $145,404.30 against a hardcoded $86,742.19. C-034 requires a $357 partial reduction on a dinner attended only by firm staff, which §5.7 disallows in full. C-045 divides a dinner of at least three people by two. Under the all-pass metric, each of these alone would zero a correct answer. C-019, C-050 and C-052 are debatable. The rubric also misses two real violations: Line 37 ($59 per person against the $50 lunch cap) and Line 43 (a routine video-conferencing license, which §5.8 treats as overhead). No criterion fixes the total reduction figure, so these gaps would not cause misgrading.

sol_verdicts.reason: I re-summed the Disbursements sheet: 47 lines (G2:G48) total $145,404.30, and G50 is a hardcoded $86,742.19. C-041 passes only a report that finds a $0.11 gap, so a solver that adds correctly and reports $58,662.11 fails. C-050 accepts the stated $86,742.19, which most reports will quote. It fails only a report that gives just the true sum, and it wrongly calls $86,742.30 the arithmetic sum. So C-050 is arguable, not confirmed.

All five Line 38 attendees are HWK personnel. §5.7 says meals attended solely by Firm personnel are not reimbursable, so the correct reduction is the full $612. C-034 requires about $357, allowing $255 for three supposedly eligible firm lawyers, and it fails the correct answer. C-032 rests on the same wrong premise, but a solver who says every attendee, summer associates included, is ineligible should still pass. So C-032 is arguable.

Invoice D41 reads 'C. Aldridge and M. Beale, with plaintiff's counsel', so at least three people dined. $247/3 = $82.33, under the $85 cap. C-045 requires the per-person figure $247/2 = $123.50, a headcount the record contradicts. A careful solver will either find no cap violation or reject the meal on eligibility grounds, and fails either way.

The pre-approval log (Entry 2, Feb 12 email) says Cha's approval for the $25K threshold 'has been obtained', with a $35,000 cap. The real gap is the missing GC sign-off for the $5,900 overage. C-019's wording implies the $25K GC threshold was never met. Most solvers will mention GC approval and pass, but one that says only that the threshold was satisfied could fail.

§5.7(b) makes meals with 'parties relevant to the Matter' eligible, and the entertainment clause turns on substantive case work. A settlement dinner with plaintiff's counsel can reasonably qualify. C-044 passes only a report that flags the meal as entertainment or as failing the attendee test. A solver that finds it eligible, or flags it only for the missing attendee names required by §5.7 Descriptions, falls between its PASS and FAIL conditions.

findings.title: C-044 assumes a settlement dinner with plaintiff's counsel is presumptively entertainment or ineligible, but §5.7(b) covers parties relevant to the Matter
findings.explanation: §5.7(b) makes meals with 'parties relevant to the Matter' eligible. The entertainment clause turns on whether substantive case work is conducted with third parties, and a settlement discussion is substantive. A competent reviewer could find Line 40 eligible, or flag it only because the description omits attendee names and titles. That report is neither 'not flagged at all' nor flagged on the grounds C-044's PASS text names, so judges may disagree.

findings.suggested_fix: Pass any report that flags Line 40 for review on any ground, including incomplete attendee documentation or uncertain eligibility.

final.changes_from_blind: I adopted C-044 as arguable (new O4) from Sol arguable/1. §5.7(b)'s 'parties relevant to the Matter' clause makes a settlement dinner with plaintiff's counsel plausibly eligible, which I had missed in the blind pass. I made the C-032 and C-033 statuses explicit inside O2: C-034 is problematic, C-032 and C-033 are arguable. I disagree with Sol on C-050: it is arguable, not confirmed, because the stated total is accepted. I dropped no blind findings. C-052 (arguable) is not in Sol's audit and I keep it.
final.overall: The rubric tracks the guidelines and pre-approval log accurately for most line items. Three criteria would fail correct work under the all-pass metric. C-041 depends on a $0.11 total discrepancy that the spreadsheet does not contain: the lines sum to $145,404.30 against a hardcoded $86,742.19. C-034 requires a $357 partial reduction on a dinner attended only by firm staff, which §5.7 disallows in full. C-045 divides a dinner of at least three people by two. Sol and I agree on all three. C-019, C-032, C-033, C-044, C-050 and C-052 are debatable. The rubric also omits real violations (the Line 37 lunch over the cap, and the Line 43 conferencing license, which is overhead), but no criterion fixes a total reduction, so those gaps do not cause misgrading.
final.coverage: I re-checked Sol's five findings against the record. I recomputed the 47 disbursement lines ($145,404.30) and confirmed that G50 is hardcoded at $86,742.19. I re-read the §5.7 attendee, entertainment and description text, the Line 38 and Line 40 descriptions, and pre-approval log Entry 2 (Hartsfield GC approval, $35K cap). I re-read the target criteria: C-019, C-032, C-033, C-034, C-041, C-044, C-045, C-050 and C-052. I carried forward my blind-pass review of all 57 criteria. No external legal authority applies, since this is the interpretation of a private billing guideline.
